items.title: The Ekho AI Sales Agent Is Officially Live
items.summary: The AI Sales Agent answers on your website and over text in under five seconds, at any hour, and it can carry a conversation through to a completed purchase. Here is everything it does, and how it compares.

items.title: Two-Way Lightspeed CRM Sync Is Live
items.summary: Two-way sync with Lightspeed CRM is live. Leads, customers and sales activity move in both directions, so the CRM remains the system of record and your team keeps working where it already works.

items.title: The Sales Agent Now Works Your Dormant CRM Leads
items.summary: Leads that arrive from your CRM can now be worked by the Sales Agent, on the follow-up schedule you already use, without anyone assigning them.

items.title: Welcoming Ethan Poortenga, Founding Product Manager
items.summary: Ethan Poortenga joins as founding Product Manager. He was the founding PM at Hang, growing it from a handful of customers to hundreds, and led both product and design there.

items.title: Welcoming Tommy Xue, AI Product Manager
items.summary: Tommy Xue joins as AI Product Manager. He led internal AI efforts at DoorDash and built the data platform behind their newer verticals, including tooling that put AI in the hands of non-technical teams.

items.title: Welcoming Eugenio Garza Garcia, Forward Deployed Engineer
items.summary: Eugenio Garza Garcia joins as a Forward Deployed Engineer. He led the sports vertical at Polymarket and owned settlements and disputes across most of the platform's volume, after two and a half years at BCG.

items.title: Welcoming Ekho's General Counsel: Justin Black
items.summary: Justin Black joins as General Counsel. He spent nearly five years at Carvana across dealer licensing, government affairs and lending compliance, and five years before that as a state regulator.

items.title: Where We Have Been
items.summary: Ekho spends time on customers' floors rather than on calls about them. This is where the team has been recently, from Las Vegas to Barcelona, and what those visits changed.

items.title: Text Buyers From the Portal, With Photos and Video
items.summary: Texting is now native to the Admin Portal, with photo and video attachments. A walkaround, a spec sheet or a colour a buyer asked about can be sent from inside the conversation, and a web chat can continue over SMS.

items.title: A Redesigned Widget, and Pre-Qualification on Your Terms
items.summary: The widget is rebuilt around booking a call, booking an appointment and getting pre-qualified, which cuts the taps between browsing and a confirmed time. Stores can now turn on pre-qualification and set their own approval threshold from the Admin Portal.

items.title: Automated Lead Routing Is Live
items.summary: Automated lead routing settles three questions without anyone assigning work by hand: which leads are eligible, who they go to, and what happens when nobody responds. Routing lives in the Admin Portal and covers sales, service and parts.

items.title: Checkmate in Plain Sight: How RumbleOn Bought the Powersports Industry While Nobody Was Watching
items.summary: Five years before Carvana started buying Stellantis franchises, an asset-light online platform quietly acquired the largest powersports dealer network in North America. The RumbleOn + RideNow deal rewrote the category in plain sight, and the operating-model gap it opened is one independent dealers can still close.

items.title: The DMS Is Not Dead. It’s Just Doing the Wrong Job.
items.summary: The dealer management system is one of the most useful pieces of software in the store, and one of the most overloaded. For twenty years it has been asked to be five products at once and blamed for the four jobs it was never built for. This is an open letter arguing the DMS gets its credibility back the moment it goes home to the work it does best.

items.title: The Greeter Problem
items.summary: A well-run dealership greets every walk-in within seconds, but most websites answer after-hours buyers with a contact form and a promise. That gap between the physical welcome and the digital one is where real intent leaks to the dealer down the road.

items.title: The Two Problems Killing Powersports Growth
items.summary: Dealers are leaking leads they already paid for, and the industry is aging out of its own buyer base. On the NPDA Partner Webinar Series, I walked through the data behind both problems and what dealers can actually do about them. This piece distills that conversation.

items.title: Dealers Don’t Have a Vendor Problem. They Have a Partner Problem. This Is Your Wake-Up Call.
items.summary: Your stack is seventeen vendors tall and not one of them is on your side. The OEM that used to be your partner has quietly become a vendor pointed the other direction. The next decade belongs to dealers who find a counterparty whose paycheck only moves when theirs does.

items.title: The Complete Guide to AI Sales Agents for Vehicle Dealerships (2026)
items.summary: Agentic AI is the first dealership tooling that can credibly own a complete pre-sale funnel, not just a slice of it. This guide shows principals and GMs what an AI Sales Agent actually does, how it differs from chatbots and AI BDC tools, and the five criteria that separate a real platform from the next vendor email.

items.title: Connect Salesforce Yourself, and See Every Lead Land
items.summary: Salesforce is now a self-serve connection in Settings, with your own field mapping, rather than something Ekho configured for you. Every lead then carries its forwarding status, and a link that opens that record in your CRM.

items.title: Vendor Stacks Are Dead. Long Live the DealershipOS.
items.summary: Almost every product on a dealer’s software stack was designed for a system-of-record dealer and a Saturday walk-in buyer. Neither exists anymore. The vendor stack is the obituary; the DealershipOS, a single operating layer holding the ledger, the conversation surface, the transaction engine, and the storefront, is the replacement.

items.title: The Sales Agent Speaks to the Brands You Actually Carry
items.summary: Each rooftop records the brands and categories it carries, and the Sales Agent answers from that. A buyer asking about a brand you do not sell gets a straight answer and a route to what you do sell.

items.title: AI Isn’t Coming for Your Job. It’s Coming for the Way You Worked Yesterday.
items.summary: AI is not erasing dealership jobs. It is erasing the parts of those jobs that were never the high-value work. The reps, advisors, and managers who trade the employee mindset for an entrepreneurial one will build careers, brands, and earning power that did not exist five years ago.

items.title: What is an AI Agent, and What Can It Do for My Dealership? The Complete Guide to How AI Agents Make You More Money
items.summary: Most dealers can't tell the difference between an AI agent, a chatbot, and an outsourced BDC, and that confusion costs money. This guide defines AI agency in plain dealer language, maps the three surfaces it shows up on, and walks through the five places it changes a dealership's unit economics.

items.title: The Unbundling Is Over. The Rebundling Has Begun.
items.summary: The dealership stack has grown for twenty years because specialized vendors were worth the integration cost. That math has flipped. Here is why the pile is starting to collapse, and which two pieces come off your desk this quarter.

items.title: How Do I Sell Vehicles Online? The Complete Guide to Financing, Titling, and Registration in All 50 States
items.summary: Most digital retail tools stop at the lead, then hand the deal back to the dealership to finish on paper. A real online vehicle transaction has to run financing, F&I, tax, titling, registration, signing, and fraud end to end, configured for all 50 states. This guide walks the full transaction stack and the eight questions that separate real infrastructure from a checkout button.

items.title: Your Store Can Now Run More Than One F&I Provider
items.summary: A dealership account can hold several F&I coverage providers at once, each with its own products, and the buyer still sees one menu.

items.title: The $50B Dealer Tax: What Your Stack Really Costs
items.summary: Every titled-vehicle dealership in the country runs a pile of sixteen vendor categories that costs $170,000 to $300,000 a year per rooftop and still fails to answer the buyer or close the deal as a system. Two of those layers, the lead funnel and the back office, are collapsible this quarter with software that already ships. Running both recovers $70,000 to $200,000 a year per store.

items.title: You’re Paying for the Traffic. You’re Answering 1.5% of It.
items.summary: Every dealership watches cost per lead. Almost none watch how few visitors ever get answered: the average site converts 1.5% to 2%, and only about 5% of buyers can finish online. The next advantage isn’t paying more for traffic, it’s answering and closing the traffic you already have.

items.title: Follow-Up Schedules Are Live
items.summary: Follow-up schedules let the Sales Agent re-engage buyers automatically after a conversation ends. You choose which leads qualify and when each message goes out, and the sequence stops on its own when the buyer replies, books, or opts out.

items.title: 20 Email Marketing Mistakes Vehicle Dealerships Need to Stop Making in 2026
items.summary: Email is still the highest-ROI channel a dealership owns. It is also the easiest to waste. Here is the 2026 fix list for motorcycle, powersports, marine, RV, and auto stores.

items.title: Every Rooftop Gets Its Own Sales Agent
items.summary: A dealer group now runs a parent account with a child account for every rooftop, so each store gets an agent configured for that store while the group keeps one standard.

items.title: Ad Conversion Tracking, Across Every Platform You Run
items.summary: Ekho reports the real checkout funnel to the ad platforms a dealership already runs. Six platforms are supported and configured per rooftop, and the conversions they receive are down-funnel milestones rather than page views.

items.title: Facebook Ads Are Bleeding Dealership Budgets. Here’s the Fix.
items.summary: How motorcycle, powersports, marine, RV, and auto dealers can turn Meta ads into qualified leads, VDP traffic, fixed-ops revenue, and sold units, instead of expensive impressions. Meta ads still reach buyers earlier, more often, and across more devices than almost any channel a dealership runs. That is exactly the problem. Cheap reach is not the same as a sold unit, and most dealer accounts are quietly burning budget on creative the algorithm can no longer optimize, campaigns it cannot learn ...

items.title: Local SEO for Vehicle Dealerships: How to Win “Near Me” Search in 2026
items.summary: Motorcycle, powersports, RV, marine, and auto dealers live and die by a 60-90 minute drive radius. This is the operational playbook for ranking in Google Maps, the Local Pack, and AI-driven “near me” results.

items.title: The 800-Pound Gorilla Just Got a Franchise License
items.summary: Carvana spent $160M acquiring franchise dealerships and turned one into the top-selling CDJR dealer in America. You can’t compete on price or inventory. Here are the three battlegrounds that matter.

items.title: The Sales Agent Now Runs on Your Corporate Site, Tethered to Your Dealers
items.summary: A manufacturer's own site can now run a Sales Agent that speaks only for that brand and hands each buyer to the nearest authorized dealer, who picks the conversation up with their own agent.

items.title: Promotions and Discounts That Reach the Deal
items.summary: Promotions are configured in the Admin Portal and applied in checkout. Dealers and manufacturers each set their own, and the offers a buyer qualifies for are priced into the deal rather than advertised beside it.

items.title: How We Rebuilt ekho.com with AI in a Week
items.summary: We migrated our entire corporate website off Webflow in about a week using Claude Code. 150+ URLs, 26 content collections, 327+ content files. This is the story of how it went, including the part where the first attempt almost killed the project, and what it means for dealer websites.

items.title: What Buyers Actually Say to an AI Sales Agent at 2:14pm on a Sunday
items.summary: The most useful thing about an AI Sales Agent isn't what it does - it's what it surfaces. This piece walks through two real, anonymized AI Sales Agent conversations from powersports dealerships - one a 15-minute Sunday-afternoon trade-in conversation that ended in a Tuesday showroom appointment, one a 9:37am inventory check that turned into a same-day phone call in three minutes - and pulls out what the back-and-forth reveals about how buyers actually want to be sold to.

items.title: Why “Online Vehicle Sales” Usually Breaks at Checkout
items.summary: Most digital-retail tools — and marketplace “Buy Now” buttons — quietly hand the deal back to the dealer’s back office the moment anything real has to happen. This piece walks through the six places online vehicle sales actually break (financing, stipulations, F&I, tax, titling, signing) in the order they show up in a deal, what each one costs the dealer, and what real checkout-to-keys infrastructure has to absorb instead.

items.title: Moto Morini Deploys Ekho's AI Sales Agent Across U.S. Website and Dealer Network
items.summary: Moto Morini, the legendary Italian motorcycle manufacturer, has deployed Ekho's AI Sales Agent on motomoriniusa.com to engage and qualify buyers around the clock. The AI handles buyer conversations in real time — answering product questions, qualifying purchase intent, and routing ready-to-buy leads to the nearest dealer across Moto Morini's growing U.S. dealer network.

items.title: The end of the price-on-the-windshield era
items.summary: The FTC’s March 2026 warning letters to 97 auto dealership groups marked a turning point: the agency is enforcing total-price disclosure case by case, and OEMs in powersports, marine, RV and LSV are already advising dealers to revisit how they advertise. This piece breaks down where dealers actually get exposed, why the same patterns extend across every titled-vehicle segment, and how disclosure-by-design turns compliance into a byproduct of a cleaner buyer experience.

items.title: Accessories Drive Margin. Why Aren't They in Every Deal?
items.summary: Parts and accessories carry 32.6% gross margin, vs. 3 to 8% on new vehicles. Most of those dollars never make it into the deal. Ekho just made accessories a built-in step of every vehicle purchase.

items.title: The Knowledge Hub Is Live
items.summary: The Knowledge Hub is live. Upload any number of documents to the Admin Portal and the Sales Agent answers from them on web chat and over SMS, so buyers get your dealership's answer rather than a generic one.

items.title: Condition and History Reports Are Live on Used Inventory
items.summary: Used listings now carry cosmetic, mechanical, title and history, and dealer warranty reports. A dealership records them once against the unit and decides which ones buyers see, so a remote buyer can judge a used vehicle before they commit to it.

items.title: Capturing Customers Who Don't Want to Come In
items.summary: At AIM Expo's Dealer Excellence main stage, Ekho co-founder Rowan Mockler shared data and perspective on why the powersports industry needs to meet younger buyers where they are — online. From the aging buyer demographic to the lifetime value of a first-time online purchaser, this piece distills the key takeaways for dealers looking to future-proof their business.

items.title: Ekho Named to the 2026 Powersports Business Nifty 50 as the Top-Ranked Dealer Tech Platform
items.summary: Ekho has been named to the 2026 Powersports Business Nifty 50, ranking #16 overall and earning the top spot among dealership technology platforms. The recognition highlights Ekho's impact on dealer profitability through its Sales Agent, AI-native dealer websites, 50-state transaction engine, and unified dealer platform.

items.title: Announcing the Dealer Website Grader
items.summary: Ekho has launched a free Dealer Website Grader to help dealerships understand how visible they are in AI search. With over 30% of buyers already using tools like ChatGPT to research where to buy, the grader evaluates AI visibility, SEO performance, technical site health, and local competitor rankings—giving dealers a clear score and actionable steps to improve their presence in AI-driven discovery.

items.title: Intelligent Inventory Merchandising is Live
items.summary: This release introduces Intelligent Inventory Merchandising, Ekho’s AI system that automatically matches and enriches dealer inventory to power autonomous titling and registration. By identifying, normalizing, and merchandising vehicles—even with inconsistent source data—the platform eliminates manual inventory mapping, accelerates onboarding, and improves vehicle discovery. Dealers benefit from faster processing and better search performance, while buyers experience a smoother path from research to road-ready.

items.title: Embedded F&I is Now Live
items.summary: Ekho’s new Protection Menu brings F&I directly into the checkout experience—online or in-store—so dealers can present curated coverage bundles in just a few clicks. Powered by dynamic logic, it adapts in real time to each buyer and dealer, delivering personalized protection options without slowing down the sale. The result is higher penetration, fewer handoff gaps, and a seamless, transparent experience that keeps both dealers and buyers in control.

items.title: Turn Browsers Into Buyers: Ekho’s New Lead Capture Flow
items.summary: Ekho’s new Lead Capture feature connects online interest with in-store sales. Instead of losing high-intent shoppers who stop short of checkout, dealers can now convert them seamlessly through a “Buy In-Person” option. Each lead is verified, logged, and instantly shared with your store—turning potential buyers into real customers. Built on a new modular checkout architecture, the system adapts dynamically across channels, keeping every potential sale in sight and every team in sync.
